why.text: A hot, dry, sunny Mediterranean south coast, sheltered from cold northern winds by mountains, on poor sandy and stony soils with Atlantic influence.

styles.text: Red and white wines; the spec sets minimum alcohol of 12% for reds and 11.5% for whites.

climate.text: Markedly Mediterranean: hot, dry and not very windy, with very small temperature swings and over 3000 hours of sun a year. The vineyards themselves feel the Atlantic and are battered by winds, so they get higher humidity and bigger temperature swings, and harvests are usually later.

soil.text: Poor, stony, low-fertility soils: sandstone-based lithosols, sandy regosols, red or yellow Mediterranean soils and podzolised coarse sands.

tastes.text: Whites: delicate and soft, with warm-zone aroma and some minerality. Reds: ruby, generally more robust and tannic, velvety, light-bodied, slightly acidic and very fruity.

why.text: A hot, dry, sunny Mediterranean climate with over 3,000 sun hours a year, sandy and sandstone soils, and sea influence from the Atlantic and the Alvor estuary.

styles.text: Reds and whites only, with at least 12% alcohol for reds and 11.5% for whites.

climate.text: Markedly Mediterranean: hot, dry, little wind, very small temperature swings, and over 3,000 hours of sun a year. Mountains shelter it from cold northern winds and the land faces south in an amphitheatre.

soil.text: Lithosols from sandstone and Silves grés, sandy regosols, red or yellow Mediterranean sandstone soils, and podzolised soils of coarse sands and sandstones.

tastes.text: Whites: balanced, delicate and soft, with some floral notes. Reds: velvety, full-bodied, very fruity, sometimes floral, low in acidity, with noticeable alcohol.

why.text: A hot, dry, very sunny Mediterranean amphitheatre facing south, sheltered from cold northern winds by mountains, on sandstone and sandy soils.

climate.text: Strongly Mediterranean: hot, dry, little wind, very small temperature swings, and more than 3000 hours of sun a year.

soil.text: Sandstone-based soils: Silves sandstone (grés de Silves), sandy regosols, red or yellow Mediterranean soils, and podzolised soils of sand and coarse sandstone.

tastes.text: Easy to drink and long-lived. Whites: robust yet soft, very fruity, fairly dry with body. Reds: velvety, full-bodied, fruity, not very floral, low in acidity, warm.

why.text: Sandy, low-lying vineyards sheltered from wind, in a hot, dry Mediterranean climate with very even temperatures and over 3000 sun hours a year.

climate.text: Clearly Mediterranean: hot, dry, little wind, very small temperature swings, over 3000 sun hours a year. A mountain barrier blocks cold northern winds and the land faces south. Little rain and many warm hours mean harvest starts earlier than in other regions.

soil.text: Sandy soils: lithic soils on sandstone, regosols, red or yellow Mediterranean soils on sandstone, and podzolised soils on coarse sands.

altitude.text: Relatively low elevations with no pronounced relief.

tastes.text: Whites: delicate, soft, aromatic and light-bodied, with a warm-region finish and some complexity. Reds: easy to drink, velvety, medium-bodied, fruity, low in tannin, slightly acidic.
